text:
julia_sales: Hey team — customer wants to run an LLM POC in their Azure VNet using ExpressRoute + PrivateLink to our Private deployment. They're asking for a DMZ egress architecture that preserves client IP for telemetry and allows TLS-inspect in the perimeter for security scanning. Any patterns/recs? :thinking:

sam_network: Short answer: two viable patterns. 1) Interface PrivateLink endpoints -> simple, secure, but original client src IP not preserved end-to-end. 2) Transit via a DMZ NVA/proxy + explicit routing -> preserves client IP if you avoid SNAT, but adds ops/complexity. Tradeoffs: observability vs cost/complexity.

anna_netops: Ops note: if they require TLS inspection we usually terminate at the perimeter firewall (Palo/CheckPoint) and re-encrypt toward our endpoint. That requires cert distribution and policy for MITM certs. If they want TLS passthrough keep it simple but you lose visibility.

mike_security: From the security questionnaire side we need the following artefacts: egress port list + IP ranges, expected TLS CNs/SANs, whether mTLS is supported, and KMS/HSM options. Also confirm logging retention and what we can share (token-level request metadata for Private/Dedicated). :white_check_mark:

julia_sales: They also asked for rough pricing guidance comparing PrivateLink vs Transit+NAT vs Azure Firewall for the POC. Anything quick I can send?

sam_network: Rough guidance (high level):
- PrivateLink: per-endpoint hourly + per-GB processing; lowest infra ops for small POC traffic.
- Transit + NAT Gateway: NAT GW hourly + per-GB egress; can be cheaper at sustained scale but adds a NAT hop.
- Azure Firewall: fixed hourly + data processing; good if they need centralized policy and TLS-inspect features.
For a week-long POC with low traffic PrivateLink usually lowest total.

anna_netops: Practical checklist I can give them to unblock networking team:
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to our service FQDN/IPs (we'll provide exact ranges)
- Allow UDP/TCP 53 for DNS if they override internal DNS to point at PrivateLink
- Ensure MTU checks if ExpressRoute + VPN coexist (verify 1500 vs 850 for GRE/VXLAN cases)
- Allow UDP 123 to NTP
- Open management ports only to jumpbox subnets (not public)
```

sam_network: Note: "preserve client IP" semantics differ: PrivateLink hijacks flow to endpoint -> source IP becomes the calling interface IP (not original end host). If they must see orig IP, options:
1) run an ingress proxy in their spoke that forwards requests preserving X-Forwarded-For header to us (app-level).
2) deploy mTLS client certs so we can associate a cert/identity to the request.
Neither is automatic with PrivateLink.

mike_security: For the questionnaire we can provide this allowed-controls snippet they can paste into their form:
```
- Transport: TLS 1.2+ between customer and Redwood endpoints; mTLS optional for Private deployments
- Key mgmt: customer-managed KMS supported for Private; Redwood can integrate with customer HSM for enterprise
- Logging: Request-level metadata (no raw PII) available for Dedicated/Private with configurable retention
- Audit: Access logs, model/version used, token counts available on request for compliance review
```

julia_sales: Great. Can someone drop a one-page diagram and sample firewall/NSG rules I can attach to the exec summary by EOD? Customer legal/security expects it with the SOW. :pray:

anna_netops: I'll produce a diagram + sample rules. Example Azure Firewall SNAT/NAT rule snippet I'll include and a Palo Alto security policy example.

deploy-bot: ticket #POC-4823 created for network handoff — assignee: anna_netops

sam_network: Quick test hack for customer to validate connectivity: stand up tiny VM in a spoke, curl our private FQDN and capture response headers. Also capture `tcpdump` on the spoke-proxy to confirm source IP translation behavior. Example test: `curl -v https://private.redwood.example/ --resolve private.redwood.example:443:10.10.1.5`

julia_sales: Thanks all — I'll forward this to the customer now and ask for confirmation on cert policy. Please join customer call tomorrow 11am PT if available.

mike_security: I'll prep questionnaire answers and a short note on acceptable MITM policies. See you on the call.
